# Problem 1
```{r}
data("ny_noaa")

noaa_missing =
  ny_noaa |>
  summarise(
    prop_prcp_na = mean(is.na(prcp)),
    prop_snow_na = mean(is.na(snow)),
    prop_snwd_na = mean(is.na(snwd)),
    prop_tmax_na = mean(is.na(tmax)),
    prop_tmin_na = mean(is.na(tmin))
  )
```
The `ny_noaa` dataset contains daily weather observations from `r n_distinct(ny_noaa$id)` New York state weather stations spanning from `r min(ny_noaa$date)` to `r max(ny_noaa$date)`, with `r format(nrow(ny_noaa), big.mark = ",")` rows and `r ncol(ny_noaa)` columns. Key variables include weather station identifier (`id`), observation date (`date`), precipitation in tenths of millimeters (`prcp`), snowfall in millimeters (`snow`), snow depth in millimeters (`snwd`), and maximum and minimum temperatures in tenths of degrees Celsius (`tmax` and `tmin`). Missing data is a substantial issue because many stations only record a subset of meteorological variables: `tmax` and `tmin` are each missing in `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * noaa_missing$prop_tmax_na)` and `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * noaa_missing$prop_tmin_na)` of observations, `snwd` is missing in `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * noaa_missing$prop_snwd_na)`, `snow` is missing in `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * noaa_missing$prop_snow_na)`, and `prcp` is missing in `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * noaa_missing$prop_prcp_na)`.

```{r}
noaa_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  separate(
    date,
    into = c("year", "month", "day"),
    sep = "-",
    convert = TRUE
  ) |>
  mutate(
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10
  )

snow_top =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(!is.na(snow)) |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

kable(
  snow_top,
  col.names = c("Snowfall (mm)", "Observations"),
  caption = "Top 5 Most Commonly Observed Snowfall Values"
)
```

I separated `date` into integer `year`, `month`, and `day` variables, and converted `prcp` from tenths of millimeters to millimeters (`mm`) as well as `tmax` and `tmin` from tenths of degrees Celsius to degrees Celsius (`°C`), so that precipitation, snowfall, and snow depth are all measured in `mm` and temperatures in `°C`. For snowfall, the most commonly observed value is `0` mm (`r format(snow_top$n[1], big.mark = ",")` observations), because snow does not fall on the vast majority of days across the year in New York State. The next most common values are `25` mm, `13` mm, `51` mm, and `76` mm, which correspond to historical measurements recorded in imperial inches (1.0 inch = 25.4 mm, 0.5 inch = 12.7 mm, 2.0 inches = 50.8 mm, and 3.0 inches = 76.2 mm) and subsequently rounded to the nearest millimeter.

```{r}
jan_july_tmax =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7), !is.na(tmax)) |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c(1, 7),
      labels = c("January", "July")
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarise(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(jan_july_tmax, aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.15, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.8, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), color = "firebrick", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Station-Level Average Maximum Temperature in January and July (1981-2010)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average Maximum Temperature (°C)"
  )
```

The two-panel plot shows a clear seasonal separation: average maximum temperatures in January generally fluctuate between -10 °C and 10 °C (centered near 0 °C), whereas July average maximum temperatures stay much warmer and more tightly clustered between 20 °C and 32 °C (centered near 27 °C). Across stations, year-to-year fluctuations move in parallel, reflecting statewide warm and cold years. Several notable outliers appear in both panels, most prominently an abnormally cold July station-year observation in 1988 (`USC00308962` at 13.95 °C) and an extremely cold January station-year observation in 1982 (`USC00301723` at -13.44 °C).
